svg.title: Contracts and Claims: The File Wins
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-contracts-and-claims-roadmap; chapter number: 12; title: Contracts and Claims: The File Wins; subtitle: Reading, pricing, answering, and documenting DLA awards and tax-free sales; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Decode the solicitation; deliverable: PR number read: 1-0-0 means an estimated IDC quantity, 700 or 090 means a firm quantity you must supply; gate: Quote only once the quantity type and inspection boxes are confirmed; week: Week 2; title: Price the bid; deliverable: Vendor cost, packaging, and inspection rolled into a 10% to 15% margin; gate: Drop 20% to 25% margins, which get underbid; week: Week 3; title: Answer traceability and counteroffers; deliverable: Re-confirmed vendor price, PDF documents on the original thread, and an Excel informal cost breakdown (6.75% profit, $261 per unit on 195 pieces); gate: Refuse a counteroffer when the math does not work; week: Week 4; title: Lock the tax and claim file; deliverable: Complete, signed, dated certificates; Texas production within 90 days of notice; a $4 grant deed for surplus-fund claims; gate: No tax-free release without a certificate matching what the customer buys; caption: Traceability requests, counteroffers, and cost-breakdown requests signal an award is close; MeND has refused government counteroffers and still won.; assumptions note: The four-week sequence is an organizing frame, not a schedule any practitioner stated; all thresholds and dollar figures are attributed claims.; note: Attributed to Tris10 @ MeND (sG-wAF0b7kQ, Y895jCYSE5A), Secureframe (v7nJCLRc0uo), Tax Expert Today (WZL5m9rfNSQ), and Overage Acquisition (X_Oq8vv4j_c).
